title: [v2 Bug] Seed `column_types` keys are matched case-sensitively against lower-cased column names
body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt v2.x compared to the latest version of dbt 1.x?
- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt v2.x
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior
On adapters where v2 folds seed column names to lower case (Postgres, Redshift, DuckDB, Salesforce, LakeCompute), a `column_types` key that matches an upper-case CSV header is silently ignored. The column gets its inferred type instead, and no warning is emitted.

### Expected Behavior
The same result as dbt 1.x: with header `EVENT_DATE` and `column_types: {EVENT_DATE: date}`, the seed has a `date` column.

### Steps To Reproduce
DuckDB, binary built from `main` at `759dbee1f` (`dbt --version`: 2.0.5):

`dbt_project.yml`
```yaml
name: duck_probe
version: "1.0"
config-version: 2
profile: duck
seeds:
  duck_probe:
    raw_upper_types:
      +column_types:
        EVENT_DATE: date
```

`seeds/raw_upper_types.csv`
```
EVENT_ID,EVENT_DATE
1,2026-09-15
2,2026-09-16
```

`dbt seed --full-refresh`, then `information_schema.columns` shows `event_date VARCHAR`. With the key written `event_date: date` instead, the column is `DATE`. (`--full-refresh` matters when the table already exists: a plain `dbt seed` truncates and reloads it, so the column keeps its previous type.)

### Where it comes from
- `crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/register_seeds.rs:96`: `adapt_schema` renames the columns with the adapter's `InferColumnNameStrategy`, and the data is persisted under that schema.
- `crates/dbt-tasks-sa/src/runnable/seed.rs:194`: the seed's agate table is read back from that file, so the macro sees `event_date`.
- The seed macros look the type up by exact name: `column_override.get(col_name, inferred_type)`.
- `check_and_warn_missing_column_types` (`seed.rs:28`) compares lower-cased names, so it finds nothing to warn about.

dbt 1.x keeps the CSV header as written, so upper-case keys match upper-case headers there.

### Proposed fix
Resolve the `column_types` keys against the agate column names case-insensitively before the materialization runs, so both `EVENT_DATE` and `event_date` work. I'm happy to open the PR.

### Environment
- OS: macOS 26 (arm64)
- dbt: v2 built from `main` at `759dbee1f` (`dbt --version`: 2.0.5), debug build

### Which database adapter are you using?
DuckDB (also reproduced on Athena with the adapter PRs from #16252)

title: state:modified misses inherited changes to grants and other merged configs
body:
Resolves #16438

### Problem

Ran into this while poking at Slim CI behavior for grants. The repro in #16438 is solid: with nested directories and inherited `+grants`, flipping an inherited grant from replace (`select: [...]`) to additive (`+select: [...]`) changes the model's effective grants but `state:modified` doesn't select the model, so CD skips it and the warehouse object keeps stale grants.

While reproducing I noticed it's actually broader than the replace-to-additive switch: pretty much any change to grants inherited from an outer directory is missed, even a plain value swap (`select: [role_b]` -> `select: [role_z]`). Only the model's innermost scope is really compared.

The reason: `state:modified` compares `unrendered_config`, and `UnrenderedConfigGenerator._update_from_config` builds that with a flat `result.update()` per fqn level. For merge-behavior fields (grants, meta, tags, pre/post-hook, ...) this keeps only the innermost scope's raw dict, while the effective config accumulates across the whole hierarchy. So an inherited change that alters the effective value but not the innermost raw value is invisible to the comparison.

### Solution

In `_update_from_config`, fold each scope in with `merge_config_dicts` (the dict-level merge already used for config call dicts — handles append/update/dict_key_append and keeps `+` markers intact) instead of the flat update. Scalar fields behave exactly like before (clobber = innermost wins), but merged fields now accumulate across scopes, so an inherited change anywhere in the chain lands in `unrendered_config` and gets compared.

Gated on `state_modified_compare_more_unrendered_values`: with the flag off the legacy flat update is kept as-is. That felt like the right place for it, since the flag already exists to push state comparison towards more unrendered values.

Trade-offs worth calling out:

- One-time effect on upgrade: nodes with inherited merged configs will diff against manifests written by older versions (whose unrendered config only had the innermost scope) and get selected once. Stable after that.
- The expectations in `tests/functional/configs/test_configs_in_schema_files.py` changed for the flag-on case, since unrendered meta/tags now include inherited entries. One quirk surfaced there: `tag_in_schema` shows up twice, because `parser/base.py` deep-merges the rendered patch dict with its unrendered form (which concatenates lists) before building the unrendered config. Left that alone — it's deterministic and pre-existing — and noted it in the fixture.

Verified with a 3-layer project matching the issue (parse, save state, flip layer_2 to additive, then `dbt ls --select state:modified --state`): the model is selected now, and a shadowed outer change that leaves effective grants identical is still (correctly) not selected. Added a functional test covering both of those plus the plain value change. Ran the defer_state, configs, artifacts and previous-version-state functional suites plus the unit tests locally against postgres.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read [the contributing guide](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and understand what's expected of me.
- [x] I have run this code in development, and it appears to resolve the stated issue.
- [x] This PR includes tests, or tests are not required or relevant for this PR.
- [x] This PR has no interface changes (e.g., macros, CLI, logs, JSON artifacts, config files, adapter interface, etc.) or this PR has already received feedback and approval from Product or DX.
- [x] This PR includes [type annotations](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html) for new and modified functions.

title: fix(databricks): stage V1 view replacements of non-view relations
body:
Resolves #16476

Port of databricks/dbt-databricks#1688

### Problem

With `use_materialization_v2` off (the default), when a Databricks view model replaces an existing table or other non-view relation, the view materialization drops the existing relation first and only then creates the view. If the view fails to build, the run fails and the table is already gone.

### Solution

Route that case through `get_replace_sql`, the replacement flow the V2 view path already uses. The view is created at the `__dbt_stg` staging relation first, then swapped in, so a failed build leaves the existing table in place. V1 and V2 now replace a relation of a different type the same way. View-over-view runs keep the existing `create or replace view` path, and grants and tags are applied in the same order as before.

The V1 branch of the vendored `view.sql` matches #1688 byte for byte. The replace-flow macros it calls (`get_replace_sql`, `create_backup`, `execute_multiple_statements`) are already vendored and match current dbt-databricks.

The `dbt-loader` view materialization test for an existing Databricks table now asserts that the first statement creates the view at the staging relation and that the table is renamed out of the way. It fails on `main`, where the view is created directly at the target after the drop.

title: fix(databricks): gate view/metric_view ALTER on matching relation type
body:
## Summary

Ports [databricks/dbt-databricks#1687](https://github.com/databricks/dbt-databricks/pull/1687) to the vendored dbt-databricks macros.

`relation_should_be_altered` now takes the target relation and only permits the in-place `view_update_via_alter` ALTER path when the existing relation's type matches the target's. Previously a metric view could be ALTERed into an ordinary view (or vice versa) when `view_update_via_alter` was enabled; these conversions now correctly replace the relation.

## Changes

- `view.sql` / `metric_view.sql`: pass `target_relation` into `relation_should_be_altered` and gate on `existing_relation.type != target_relation.type`; drop the now-redundant `(is_view or is_metric_view)` clause that the type gate subsumes.
- `dbt_macro_assets` changelog: record the sync.
- `dbt-loader` macro test `v2_update_via_alter_replaces_metric_view_with_view`: a `metric_view` -> `view` conversion with `view_update_via_alter` enabled replaces instead of ALTERing. Verified RED on the pre-port macro and GREEN after.

## Testing

`cargo test -p dbt-loader --test main materializations::view` — 8/8 Databricks view cases pass; `cargo fmt` clean.
